summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever and hypotension during dialysis, found to have MSSA bacteremia likely from his right femoral dialysis catheter. He was treated with vancomycin initially, then transitioned to cefazolin after sensitivities confirmed susceptibility. The infected catheter was removed, and after a 5-day line holiday, a new tunneled left femoral dialysis catheter was placed. Blood cultures cleared, and he completed dialysis without complications. His heart function remained stable, and no endocarditis was detected. New medications were started, including lisinopril for heart failure, atorvastatin, and adjusted phosphate binders. He was discharged to an extended care facility on outpatient antibiotics with plans for ongoing dialysis and follow-up.
